This study determines the effect of four MADRL algorithms (HAPPO, MASAC, MATD3, MAAC) on energy flexibility, CO₂ emissions and energy costs in a smart community of the Iquitos Isolated Electric System under a 4×3 quasi-experimental design on CityLearn v3 (Dec-POMDP/CTDE). Evidence comes solely from canonical Drive run madrl_v3_20260627_164047 (50 episodes; HAPPO 49/50). All evidence was recalculated exclusively from the real 50-episode results for each of the 12 treatments in run madrl_v3_20260627_164047: 600 episode rows, 668 district KPI values, 15,300 building KPI values and 204 building-behaviour summaries. Descriptively, MATD3 leads E1 (smallest flexibility deterioration, -0.0923%) and E2 (smallest CO2 increase, -0.4193%, +23,070 kgCO2), while MAAC leads E3 (smallest cost increase, -0.2675%).
